GAL.1.1-2.text: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia

GAL.1.3-5.text: Christ gave himself for our sins to rescue us

GAL.1.6-7.text: Paul is amazed that the Galatians turn to another gospel

GAL.1.8-9.text: Anyone who preaches a different gospel is under a curse

GAL.1.10-10.text: Paul wants to please God, not people

GAL.1.11-12.text: Paul received the gospel from Jesus Christ, not from men

GAL.1.13-14.text: Paul once persecuted the church of God

GAL.1.15-17.text: God called Paul to preach to the Gentiles

GAL.1.18-20.text: Paul visits Cephas in Jerusalem for fifteen days

GAL.1.21-24.text: The churches of Judea praise God because of Paul

GAL.2.1-2.text: Paul goes to Jerusalem and tells the leaders the gospel

GAL.2.3-5.text: Titus is not forced to be circumcised

GAL.2.6-8.text: The leaders accept Paul’s work among the Gentiles

GAL.2.9-10.text: James, Cephas and John welcome Paul and Barnabas

GAL.2.11-12.text: Paul opposes Cephas for avoiding Gentile believers

GAL.2.13-14.text: Paul corrects Cephas in front of everyone

GAL.2.15-16.text: People are made right by faith in Christ, not by the law

GAL.2.17-19.text: Paul says Christ does not make believers sinners

GAL.2.20-21.text: Paul lives by faith in the Son of God who loved him

GAL.3.1-3.text: Paul asks the Galatians if the law brought the Spirit

GAL.3.4-5.text: Paul asks if God works miracles by law or by faith

GAL.3.6-9.text: Those who have faith are sons of Abraham

GAL.3.10-12.text: The law brings a curse; the righteous live by faith

GAL.3.13-14.text: Christ freed us from the curse of the law

GAL.3.15-16.text: God’s promise to Abraham cannot be canceled

GAL.3.17-18.text: The law does not cancel God’s promise to Abraham

GAL.3.19-20.text: Paul explains why God gave the law

GAL.3.21-22.text: The law does not oppose God’s promises

GAL.3.23-25.text: The law was a guardian until faith came

GAL.3.26-26.text: All believers are sons of God through faith

GAL.3.27-29.text: All believers are one in Christ and heirs of Abraham

GAL.4.1-2.text: An heir who is a child is like a slave

GAL.4.3-5.text: God sent his Son to redeem people under the law

GAL.4.6-7.text: God’s Spirit makes believers sons and heirs, not slaves

GAL.4.8-9.text: Paul asks why the Galatians want to be slaves again

GAL.4.10-11.text: Paul fears for the Galatians who keep special days

GAL.4.12-14.text: The Galatians welcomed Paul like an angel of God

GAL.4.15-16.text: Paul asks if the truth made him the Galatians’ enemy

GAL.4.17-18.text: False teachers want to separate the Galatians from Paul

GAL.4.19-20.text: Paul longs to be with the Galatians, his children

GAL.4.21-23.text: Abraham had two sons, by a slave woman and a free woman

GAL.4.24-25.text: Hagar stands for the covenant of Mount Sinai and slavery

GAL.4.26-27.text: The Jerusalem above is free and is our mother

GAL.4.28-29.text: Believers are children of promise, like Isaac

GAL.4.30-31.text: Believers are children of the free woman, not the slave

GAL.5.1-2.text: Paul urges believers to stand firm in freedom

GAL.5.3-4.text: Men who are circumcised must obey the whole law

GAL.5.5-8.text: Faith working through love matters, not circumcision

GAL.5.9-10.text: Whoever troubles the Galatians will bear judgment

GAL.5.11-12.text: Paul is persecuted because he does not preach circumcision

GAL.5.13-15.text: Believers should use freedom to serve one another in love

GAL.5.16-18.text: Believers should walk by the Spirit, not the flesh

GAL.5.19-21.text: Paul lists the acts of the flesh and warns believers

GAL.5.22-24.text: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, and more

GAL.5.25-26.text: Believers should walk with the Spirit and not be proud

GAL.6.1-2.text: Believers should gently restore someone caught in sin

GAL.6.3-5.text: Each believer should test his own work and carry his load

GAL.6.6-8.text: A person reaps what he sows, from flesh or Spirit

GAL.6.9-10.text: Believers should not grow tired of doing good to all

GAL.6.11-13.text: Some people force circumcision to avoid persecution

GAL.6.14-16.text: Paul boasts only in the cross; a new creation counts

GAL.6.17-18.text: Paul bears Jesus’ marks and blesses the believers
